title: [FEATURE] Allow granular skill enable/disable within plugins to reduce startup overhead
author: pushp-42

top_comments.author: matus-d-ui42
top_comments.body:
exactly what i wanted to post !
(and claude code helped me to find this issue haha)

we made my own plugin and want this granular access to enabling and disabling some skills based on what im doing that day.

also it would be great to be able to load claude with all skills disabled during that session, so it does not load them before i disable them, but still keep the plugin enabled
e.g. claude --no-plugin-skills="my-plugin"

and please consider allowing blacklist approach too

top_comments.author: kinluek
top_comments.body:
+1 with a different framing that I think strengthens the case.

The OP's angle is **startup token cost** (4–11% wasted). Real, but for us in a focused project scope the bigger pain is **agent skill-selection quality**.

## Use case

We work in a tightly-scoped stack: Go backend + React Native/Expo + GCP + Postgres + Firebase. We have a project `CLAUDE.md` matrix (~17 rows) telling the agent which 1–3 of the ~270 listed plugin skills to load per task area.

top_comments.author: CarterPape
top_comments.body:
+1, with a concrete data point from a power-user Cloudflare workflow.

The Cloudflare plugin is a clean example of a plugin where the *plugin author's* correct choice (one comprehensive bundle) and the *user's* correct choice (load only what's relevant per session) are fundamentally in tension without this feature.
